_agentide.purpose: Publication-page standard for AgentIde. Mirrors the structure used by the browser-extension-control reference so every project in this portfolio reads as one body of work. This governs the published narrative page ONLY - the live dashboard UI is governed by standard.json + admin-standard.json.

meta.name: AgentIde Publication Standard
meta.location: Single self-contained index.html at the publication root, with design/standard.json alongside it.
meta.hosting: NOT HOSTED. Build the artefact, commit it, leave deployment as an explicit later step. Do not add a canonical URL, og:image absolute URL, or a Live: line until it is actually deployed - a canonical URL that 404s is worse than none.

styleVariant.composition: neobrutalism structure (hard 2-3px borders, visible blocky structure, bold headings) x minimalism restraint (no background texture, no filled badges everywhere, no boxy containers for everything, accent rationed)
styleVariant.whyThisProject: It is a security instrument, not a consumer product. Visible structure signals instrumentation; the minimalism restraint keeps a dense technical page readable rather than shouting.
discipline: Hard offset shadow (--shadow-hard: 5px 5px 0 var(--fg)) on AT MOST 2 element classes: the hero block and figures/diagrams. Every extra shadow dilutes the ones that earned it.
Accent colour reserved for: section numerals, inline links, focus rings, one key rule. Never a background fill.
Callouts reduced to a left border rule + label. No speech-bubble shapes, no arrows.
No background texture, no dot grid, no sticker tags.
Status/severity must always pair colour with a text label - never colour alone.

typography.heading: Space Grotesk (500, 700)
typography.loadVia: Google Fonts link with preconnect; font-family stack falls back to system sans if offline.
typography.usage: Headings Space Grotesk. Prose Inter. Anything that is a path, service name, registry key, command, port or code is JetBrains Mono. This distinction is load-bearing in a security doc - literal values must be typographically separable from prose.

accent.rationale: Amber/oxide, NOT the standard placeholder #4F46E5. This is a defensive-security instrument; an indigo/violet accent is explicitly banned by standard.json and also reads as generic SaaS. Amber carries the 'instrumentation / caution' register the subject needs.
accent.usage: Section numerals, links, focus ring, one key rule, the key figure. Nothing else.

statusPalette._rule: Each status always ships colour + text label + optional glyph. Colour alone is a WCAG failure and is banned by core.accessibility.neverConveyMeaningByColorAlone.

fail.label: FAIL
fail.meaning: Vendor did not detect or did not resist

partial.label: PARTIAL
partial.meaning: Detected but a control was evaded

na.label: N/A
na.meaning: Technique not applicable to this endpoint

modes.both: Light and dark are BOTH implemented via prefers-color-scheme AND a manual toggle. The toggle is persisted to localStorage. Dark is designed, not inverted.
modes.darkAccentReason: The amber needs lightening to clear 4.5:1 against neutral-900. Use this value, not the light-mode accent, in dark.

spacing.rule: Only these nine values. No one-off pixels.

structure.singleFile: One index.html. CSS in a <style> block, no build step, no framework, no external JS beyond an optional theme toggle.
structure.why: The reference project proves this format works for a static publication: it is diffable, reviewable in a PR, and needs no hosting pipeline. A dual-use security write-up should stay auditable in git.
requiredSections: Hero - one-line what it is, the dual-use warning
How an assessment runs - the lifecycle
Safety and authorisation - non-negotiable, stated early
Limitations and out of scope - honest section
structure.sectionNumeralPattern: Sections are numbered in the margin with the accent colour, e.g. a mono '03' label. This is the primary use of the accent.

contentSafety._rule: This is the most important section of this standard. AgentIde stops security services, kills vendor processes, deletes vendor binaries, and installs a hardened SYSTEM service that resists removal. A public write-up must not become a copy-paste EDR-evasion runbook.
mandatory: A prominent dual-use warning ABOVE THE FOLD, not buried in a footer. The reference project's README does this; the page must too.
Explicit 'authorised testing only' statement with the legal framing (systems you own or have written authorisation to test).
Describe WHAT each control does and WHY it exists. Do NOT publish a parameterised, ready-to-run evasion sequence.
Publish the assessment METHODOLOGY and the scoring model. Withhold copy-paste operational detail that would let an unauthorised actor run a full undetected assessment.
Never publish real customer endpoint data, real tokens, real internal IPs, or organisation names. All examples must be RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 reserved values.
No live dashboard URLs, no real agent token values, no AGENT_TOKEN strings even as placeholders that look real.
contentSafety.reviewGate: Before any hosting decision, re-read contentSafety.mandatory against the rendered page. A hosted page is public and indexable.

accessibility.focusVisible: 2px solid accent with 2px offset, on every interactive element
accessibility.landmarks: header / main / footer, one h1, no skipped heading levels

motion.rule: Every animation must confirm a cause and effect. Nothing decorates.

responsive.requirement: No horizontal overflow at 320px. Tables scroll in their own container rather than widening the page. This was a real fix in the reference project's history - do not regress it.

accessibility.code: Every code block must be selectable text, never an image. Never rely on syntax colour alone for meaning.

required: favicon as an inline data: URI SVG so the page has zero external asset dependencies
deferredUntilHosted: link rel=canonical with an absolute URL
og:image pointing at an absolute hosted asset URL
JSON-LD url and image absolute fields
metadata._reason: These are placeholders that resolve to nothing until deployment. Ship them at deploy time, not before.

authorAttribution.pattern: Name plus GitHub profile link, per the reference project. Where two people authored a piece, both get equal billing - never a 'with thanks to'.

assetPolicy.generatedArtwork: Cover/diagram images are optional and are produced separately. They are NOT required for the page to be complete - the reference project shipped text-first and added artwork in a later commit.
assetPolicy.optimisation: If artwork is added, keep each under ~1MB and commit it; multi-MB PNGs should be compressed first. The reference project's quantity-vs-allowlist figure is 3MB, which is the upper bound not to exceed.

commitHygiene.oneConcernPerCommit: The reference history is granular: restyle, artwork, authorship, overflow fix, post drafts each land separately. Follow that - it keeps the design evolution reviewable.
commitHygiene.doNot: Do not bundle the publication, artwork, README rewrite and unrelated code changes into one commit.
